assumptions.statement: A is a total unital monoid, Phi:A->Y is a total response map, and every compared algebraic response-compatible triple has a surjective unital q with Phi=psi q.

For the compact theorem, A is compact metrizable with jointly continuous multiplication, Y is metrizable Hausdorff, Phi is continuous, and every compared topological triple has compact Hausdorff B with q and psi continuous and q a quotient map.

The finite soft tier uses a finite DAG on finite state spaces, normalized baseline kernels, compact typed palettes inside finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes with their Euclidean evaluation topology, isolated bottom symbols, and coordinatewise right override.

Every admitted comparison is induced by invertible typed state maps preserving ordered R-input, E-mediator, and O-output roles, one compatible protocol-monoid map Theta, and one protocol-independent global boundary-response map U intertwining every protocol; time reversal, R-O exchange, and target erasure are excluded.

The released fifteen hard protocol classes and their fixed right-override response semantics are used for L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4) at passive crossover 5/12; hard nonisomorphism is not assumed and is separately proved or mapped.

Sequential randomized selectors are sampled independently, compose by convolution on the finite hard monoid, and have affine unmarked retained-law response; admitted randomized isomorphisms are affine, unital, convolution preserving, and use the single global U.

The finite standard-Borel tier starts from explicitly declared pointwise normalized kernels and standard-Borel palettes with jointly measurable evaluations; no pointwise mechanism is inferred from an almost-sure observational conditional version.

The positive topological measurable tier has compact Polish node spaces, compact metrizable palettes, isolated bottom symbols, finite-coordinate right override, and jointly Feller baseline and replacement kernels.

The circle carries normalized Haar law and heat kernels H_r with H_r H_q=H_(r+q) and Fourier eigenvalues exp(-n^2 r); 0<s<t, the mediator palette is P(T) with weak topology, preparations are K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE), and comparisons preserve ordered boundary roles, the mediator experiment, heat geometry, Theta, and one global U.

claims.statement: For every response system, two protocols are contextually equivalent exactly when every two-sided context has the same response; this relation is the largest two-sided monoid congruence contained in ker(Phi).
claims.quantifiers: For every monoid A, set Y, total Phi:A->Y, and every two-sided congruence on A contained in ker(Phi).
claims.falsifier: An in-scope pair violating equivalence or congruence, or a response-compatible congruence not contained in contextual equivalence.

claims.statement: Every response-compatible quotient triple has one unique surjective unital factor from its quotient monoid to the contextual quotient, commuting with both the raw quotient map and descended response.
claims.quantifiers: For every algebraic response-compatible triple (q,B,psi) satisfying ASM-ALGEBRAIC-RESPONSE-SYSTEM, with no finiteness assumption.
claims.falsifier: An in-scope response-compatible triple for which h(q(a))=[a] is ill-defined, not a unique surjective unital homomorphism, or fails either commuting identity.

claims.statement: When A is finite, the contextual quotient has minimum cardinality among response-compatible quotient triples, and equality of cardinalities makes the unique factor an isomorphism; minimum triples are uniquely isomorphic over A.
claims.quantifiers: For every finite monoid A and every algebraic response-compatible quotient triple over the same response system.
claims.falsifier: A finite in-scope quotient triple smaller than the contextual quotient, or an equal-cardinality factor that is not an isomorphism over A.

claims.quantifiers: For every compact metrizable response monoid and every topological response-compatible triple satisfying ASM-COMPACT-CONTINUOUS-RESPONSE.
claims.falsifier: An in-scope compact response system whose dense signature misses a contextual distinction, whose quotient is not compact metrizable, or whose descended structure is discontinuous.

claims.statement: For the fixed operational data declared below, establish the conjunction that (i) for every monoid A the two-sided contextual relation is the coarsest response-compatible congruence and its quotient has the terminal finer-to-coarser factorization property, while only for finite A it has minimum cardinality and equality of quotient cardinalities forces an isomorphism over A; (ii) under compact-metrizable continuity and quotient-map hypotheses this quotient is compact metrizable with continuous multiplication and response; (iii) finite normalized typed local-kernel replacement with palettes compact in finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes supports a compact right-override soft protocol monoid with continuous response, and the retained mediator target face of the released BSC pair has unequal exact total-variation diameters despite the same passive law; (iv) independent randomized hard protocols form an affine convolution monoid whose released BSC contextual signatures have full rank, so equal passive laws do not determine the randomized response experiment under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphism; (v) declared finite standard-Borel DAG kernels give Borel protocol responses and the compact-Polish jointly Feller finite-coordinate right-override tier gives a compact metrizable operational quotient; and (vi) with mediator palette `P(T)` in the weak topology and constant-parent kernels `K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE)`, the circle heat-kernel pair has the same passive retained law but strict one-way Blackwell comparison and strict soft response-set inclusion. Every admitted typed relabeling is induced by invertible typed state maps, a compatible protocol-monoid isomorphism `Theta`, and one protocol-independent boundary-response isomorphism `U` satisfying `Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a))` for every protocol. The BSC and circle comparison categories fix `R` as the input/parameter boundary and `O` as the output/observation boundary and forbid `R`-`O` exchange and time-reversal morphisms. No canonical raw latent/DAG realization, target-erasing arbitrary-soft result, correlated-randomization result, uncontrolled regular-conditional identification, noncompact topological quotient theorem, VFE/ELBO emergence, agency, gauge/RG extension, or ontology claim is in the target.
claims.quantifiers: For every monoid A, response set Y, response map Phi:A->Y, and algebraic response-compatible quotient triple (q,B,psi) in which q:A->B is a surjective unital monoid homomorphism, psi:B->Y is a map, and Phi=psi∘q, the algebraic contextual congruence and unique finer-to-coarser factorization conjunct is universal. Only when A is finite, the quotient has minimum cardinality among response-compatible quotient triples, and equality of cardinalities makes the factor map an isomorphism over A. For every compact metrizable monoid A with jointly continuous multiplication, metrizable Hausdorff Y, and continuous Phi, and every topological response-compatible quotient triple with B a compact Hausdorff topological monoid, q and psi continuous, and q a quotient map, the compact-quotient conjunct is universal. For every finite DAG presentation with finite state spaces and declared typed palettes J_v that are compact subsets of the corresponding finite-dimensional stochastic-kernel polytopes with Euclidean/evaluation-subspace topology, the normalized soft-replacement semantics and response continuity are universal; the unequal target-face diameters are asserted for the specified BSC models L(1/4,1/3) and L(1/3,1/4), every epsilon with 0<epsilon<1/2, and every interior pair epsilon<s_-<s_+<1-epsilon, with `R` fixed as input/parameter and `O` fixed as output/observation. For the released fifteen-class hard BSC monoids and independently randomized selectors, the affine-convolution and full-contextual-rank conjunct is asserted at passive crossover delta=5/12 under response-compatible affine unital convolution-monoid isomorphisms that preserve that ordered boundary. For every finite standard-Borel DAG with standard-Borel protocol palettes and declared jointly evaluation-measurable normalized pointwise kernel families, the Borel-response conjunct is universal; for every compact-Polish jointly Feller instance whose protocol monoid is the finite-coordinate right-override product of compact metrizable palettes and isolated bottom symbols, the compact operational quotient conjunct is universal. For the circle heat-kernel models and every 0<s<t, set `J_E=P(T)` with weak topology and `K_nu(dE|R=r)=nu(dE)`; the passive-equality, strict one-way Blackwell, compact-Feller, and strict soft-response-set conjuncts are universal in s and t, with a positive smooth strictness witness `nu_rho=H_rho(x_0,dot)` for every fixed circle point `x_0` and every 0<rho<t-s, where `dot` denotes the measure argument. Every admitted typed comparison is induced by invertible typed state maps, the compatible pushforward protocol-monoid isomorphism `Theta`, and one protocol-independent boundary-response isomorphism `U` satisfying `Phi'(Theta(a))=U(Phi(a))` for every protocol `a`. Every BSC and circle experiment comparison preserves the ordered `R`-to-`O` external boundary, declared target/type coloring, response codomain, mediator parameter experiment, circle heat geometry where applicable, and admitted morphism class; `R`-`O` exchange, time reversal, and protocol-dependent boundary intertwiners are forbidden.
